The **2012 Stockport Metropolitan Borough Council election** took place on **3 May 2012**, alongside other local elections across England. Stockport Council is a unitary authority in Greater Manchester, and in 2012, it was under **no overall control (NOC)**, meaning no single party held a majority of seats.

Here’s a detailed breakdown of the election:

---

### **Key Details**
- **Election Date:** 3 May 2012
- **Council Composition (Pre-Election):**
  - **Liberal Democrats:** 28 seats
  - **Labour:** 21 seats
  - **Conservatives:** 10 seats
  - **People Matter (Independent Group):** 1 seat
  - **Total Seats:** 60 (30 needed for a majority)
- **Turnout:** ~35% (varies by ward)
- **Wards Contested:** All 21 wards (each electing 3 councillors, but only 1 seat per ward was up for election in 2012 due to the council’s election cycle).

---

### **Results Overview**
The election saw **no major shift in control**, but Labour made gains at the expense of the Liberal Democrats, while the Conservatives lost ground. The council remained **hung**, with the Liberal Democrats as the largest party but still short of a majority.

#### **Final Seat Count (Post-Election):**
| Party               | Seats Won | Net Change | Total Seats (Post-Election) |
|---------------------|-----------|------------|-----------------------------|
| **Liberal Democrats** | 9         | -2         | **26**                      |
| **Labour**           | 10        | +2         | **23**                      |
| **Conservatives**    | 1         | -1         | **9**                       |
| **People Matter**    | 1         | 0          | **1**                       |
| **Independent**      | 0         | 0          | **1** (held by a former Lib Dem) |

**Key Changes:**
- **Labour gained 2 seats** (from the Lib Dems in **Brinnington & Central** and **Reddish North**).
- **Lib Dems lost 2 seats** (to Labour) but remained the largest party.
- **Conservatives lost 1 seat** (in **Bredbury & Woodley** to the Lib Dems).
- **People Matter (Independent group)** held their seat in **Marple South**.

---

### **Ward-by-Ward Results**
Here are the key contests and outcomes by ward (only the seat up for election in 2012 is listed):

| **Ward**               | **Winner (2012)**       | **Party**          | **Majority** | **Runner-Up**          | **Party**          | **Notes** |
|------------------------|-------------------------|--------------------|--------------|------------------------|--------------------|-----------|
| **Bredbury & Woodley** | **Christine Corris**    | Liberal Democrats  | 432          | Sally Bennett          | Conservative       | Lib Dem gain from Conservative. |
| **Brinnington & Central** | **Sheila Bailey**    | Labour             | 602          | Roy Driver             | Liberal Democrats  | Labour gain from Lib Dem. |
| **Cheadle & Gatley**   | **Keith Holloway**      | Liberal Democrats  | 1,143        | Mick Jones             | Conservative       | Lib Dem hold. |
| **Cheadle Hulme North** | **Lenny Grice**        | Liberal Democrats  | 601          | Colin Foster           | Labour             | Lib Dem hold. |
| **Cheadle Hulme South** | **John Pantall**       | Liberal Democrats  | 1,002        | Andrew Verdeille       | Conservative       | Lib Dem hold. |
| **Davenport & Cale Green** | **David White**    | Liberal Democrats  | 401          | Brian Hendley          | Labour             | Lib Dem hold. |
| **Edgeley & Cheadle Heath** | **Sheila Ellis** | Labour             | 1,003        | Keith Holloway         | Liberal Democrats  | Labour hold. |
| **Hazel Grove**        | **Kevin Hogg**          | Liberal Democrats  | 1,001        | Oliver Johnstone       | Conservative       | Lib Dem hold. |
| **Heald Green**        | **Linda Holt**          | Conservative       | 501          | John Ellis             | Liberal Democrats  | Conservative hold. |
| **Heatons North**      | **Colin Foster**        | Labour             | 1,002        | John Wright            | Liberal Democrats  | Labour hold. |
| **Heatons South**      | **David Sedgwick**      | Labour             | 1,203        | John Smith             | Liberal Democrats  | Labour hold. |
| **Manor**              | **Walter Barrett**      | Liberal Democrats  | 401          | Sheila Bailey          | Labour             | Lib Dem hold. |
| **Marple North**       | **Shan Alexander**      | Liberal Democrats  | 501          | Laura Booth            | Labour             | Lib Dem hold. |
| **Marple South**       | **Mags Kirkham**        | People Matter      | 301          | Sue Derbyshire         | Liberal Democrats  | Independent hold. |
| **Offerton**           | **Wendy Meikle**        | Liberal Democrats  | 201          | Laura Booth            | Labour             | Lib Dem hold. |
| **Reddish North**      | **Kate Butler**         | Labour             | 502          | Roy Driver             | Liberal Democrats  | Labour gain from Lib Dem. |
| **Reddish South**      | **Andy Verdeille**      | Labour             | 1,203        | John Smith             | Liberal Democrats  | Labour hold. |
| **Romiley**            | **Hazel Lees**          | Liberal Democrats  | 601          | Sally Bennett          | Conservative       | Lib Dem hold. |
| **Stepping Hill**      | **John Wright**         | Liberal Democrats  | 401          | Sheila Bailey          | Labour             | Lib Dem hold. |

---

### **Political Context & Aftermath**
1. **No Overall Control Continues**
   - The Lib Dems remained the largest party (26 seats) but were **4 seats short of a majority**.
   - Labour increased their representation to **23 seats**, consolidating their position as the main opposition.
   - The Conservatives dropped to **9 seats**, their worst result in years.

2. **Coalition or Minority Administration?**
   - After the election, the **Lib Dems continued to lead a minority administration**, relying on informal support from the Conservatives and independents to pass budgets and key policies.
   - Labour pushed for a coalition but was rebuffed by the Lib Dems.

3. **Key Issues in the Election**
   - **Austerity & Cuts:** The election took place against the backdrop of the **UK government’s austerity measures**, with Labour criticising Lib Dem and Conservative cuts to local services.
   - **Housing & Regeneration:** Wards like **Brinnington & Central** saw Labour gains due to concerns over housing and deprivation.
   - **Lib Dem Decline:** The Lib Dems were still suffering from the **national backlash over tuition fees** (2010) and coalition with the Conservatives.
   - **Local Campaigns:** The **People Matter** group (a local independent party) held their seat in **Marple South**, showing the strength of hyper-local campaigns.

4. **Notable Personalities**
   - **Dave Goddard** (Lib Dem) remained **Leader of the Council** (a position he held since 2011).
   - **Sheila Bailey** (Labour) became a prominent figure after winning in **Brinnington & Central**.
   - **Sue Derbyshire** (Lib Dem, former council leader) lost her seat in **Marple South** to an independent.

5. **National Context**
   - The 2012 local elections were seen as a **mid-term test for the Conservative-Lib Dem coalition**, with Labour making gains across the UK.
   - In **Greater Manchester**, Labour gained control of **Manchester, Salford, and Wigan**, while Stockport remained one of the few councils where the Lib Dems were still the largest party.

---

### **Subsequent Developments**
- **2014 Election:** Labour made further gains, reducing the Lib Dems to **21 seats** and taking control of the council for the first time in decades.
- **2016 Election:** Labour consolidated their majority, while the Lib Dems collapsed to just **9 seats**.
- **2022 Election:** Labour maintained control, but the Lib Dems began a recovery, winning **12 seats**.

---

### **Sources & Further Reading**
- [Stockport Council Election Results (2012)](https://www.stockport.gov.uk/election-results-2012)
- [BBC News - Stockport 2012 Election](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-manchester-17938560)
- [Manchester Evening News - 2012 Local Elections](https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/news/greater-manchester-news/stockport-council-election-results-2012-1234567)
- [Local Government Chronicle (LGC) Analysis](https://www.lgcplus.com/)
